youtube.title: Kartikeya: Born of Fire, He Led the Gods | Ramayana Ep 12
youtube.description:
The gods' commander was a newborn child. 🔥

On the bank of the Ganga, Vishvamitra went on with the Ganga's tale. While Rudra did tapas, the gods, led by Agni, went to Brahma in search of a commander. Brahma told them that Uma's curse stood, and the gods would have no sons of their own; but Agni and the sky-Ganga would bring them a commander. So on Kailasa, the gods bade Agni entrust Rudra's radiance to the Ganga. All her streams blazed, and the Ganga said she could not hold such fire. At Agni's word, she set the blaze down on a slope of Himavan. Where it touched the earth rose gold and silver (हिरण्य, as traditionally glossed), copper and iron, tin and lead, and the reeds, trees and shrubs of the mountain turned to gold. There the child was born, bright as fire. The gods asked the six Krittika stars to nurture him, and they named him Kartikeya. Still tender, the six-faced child routed the demon hosts by his own valour, and the gods, led by Agni, anointed him commander of their armies. This, said the sage, was the Ganga's account, and Kartikeya's blessed birth.

📜 On screen (Valmiki Ramayana 1.37.15, vulgate):
"Tam uvāca tato gaṅgā sarvadevapurogamam, aśaktā dhāraṇe deva tejas tava samuddhatam"
(Then the Ganga said to Agni, leader of all the gods: O god, I cannot hold your risen radiance.)
